title: Level a passive gimbal by moving ballast
instruction: Level the passive instrument platform by moving its two ballast sliders. Set the ballast with both grey brake handles in their starting positions. Pull both brake handles fully forward. Prove that the free platform returns to level after a roll tilt and after a pitch tilt. Do not move ballast or apply either brake during these proofs. Release both hands. The platform has no levelling motor.
context: An instrument platform should return to level after a disturbance without relying on an angle motor or a brake that remains applied.
setup: Use the official bimanual YAM table. Coordinates are metres in the station frame. A grey fixed metal stand has a 300 by 300 by 8 mm base. The two passive axes meet at x 0.27 and y 0 and 70 mm above the table. An 80 g roll frame is 210 mm square with 10 mm rails. A blue 200 g platform is 160 by 160 by 8 mm. Its authored mass centre is 25 mm forward and 15 mm left and 12 mm below the pivot. Two captive 100 g metal ballast blocks are each 30 by 30 by 16 mm with raised polymer grips on thin stems. Each grip is 26 by 26 by 22 mm and its centre is 60 mm above its ballast body frame. The x ballast starts 40 mm forward and 40 mm right and 8 mm below the platform frame. It travels 65 mm along x. The y ballast starts 40 mm behind and 40 mm left and 8 mm below the platform frame. It travels 50 mm along y. The grey brake caps are 24 mm cubes with mass 30 g. They start 110 mm behind the pivot and 200 mm to either side and 80 mm above the table. Each travels 20 mm along x on an ideal native guide attached to the fixed stand. Both brakes start closed. Both platform axes start at zero with limits of plus or minus 20 degrees. The source declares every primitive and mass centre. Two blue disturbance caps are 26 by 26 by 24 mm. Their centres are 80 mm above the platform pivot at local y 140 mm and local x minus 140 mm. Thin outboard stems connect them to the platform through low bars. Exact primitive dimensions are in task.py.
scoring: Both brake sliders must exceed 15 mm to free the platform. Record the two ballast positions on release. Reapplying either brake or changing either ballast more than 0.5 mm clears all proofs. First show level within 2 degrees on both axes with angular speeds below 0.04 rad/s and robot contact clear for one second. Then disturb roll beyond 8 degrees and show the same free return to level. Then disturb pitch beyond 8 degrees and show another free return to level. Each proof earns 0.25. All three proofs earn 1 when the platform remains free and clear and both grippers are open with the final one second hold and all robot contacts clear. Otherwise retain 0.25 per completed proof.
run_limit: 2400 control steps at 20 Hz. This is 120 seconds of control time.
reset_notes: Recreate the authored scene with all joint displacements at zero and clear the entire scoring history. No parts are consumed. Use the official ready pose and seed 0 with zero object jitter.
fidelity: Native articulated gravity with authored mass centres and passive damping and friction. Brakes alter velocity damping and effort limits with zero angular stiffness and zero target velocity. No levelling servo exists. Internal articulation collisions are disabled. Control stems simplify mass distribution. The demo expert reads joints and commands only robot targets. Dream receives cameras and robot state. Full limitations are in README.md.
